picks.style: vedic recitation, tanpura drone, low male chant with distant chorus, very slow, austere, cosmic
picks.why: The sages approach Manu and he answers with the world before the world: 'darkness, unperceived, as if wholly asleep on all sides'.

picks.style: sanskrit didactic chant, tanpura, hand cymbals, clear male voice, measured, steady, aphoristic
picks.why: 'A sacrifice perishes through falsehood; tapas perishes through pride' — and dharma accumulated slowly, as termites build an anthill.

picks.style: upanishadic chant, deep drone, sparse bell, grave male voice, slow, inward, spacious
picks.why: The triple staff of speech, mind and body, and the knower of the field distinguished from the doer — the metaphysical close of the book.

picks.style: roman comic monologue, tibia double pipe, lyre, rueful tenor, moderate, worldly, mock-tragic
picks.why: A whole life is not enough for a lover to learn how many ways he can be ruined — one voice, one theme, complete.

picks.style: latin comic aria, aulos, hand drum, knowing alto, brisk, conspiratorial, direct to the audience
picks.why: Phronesium explains her faked childbirth straight to the crowd — 'to a female it is a much less burden to do bad than good'.

picks.style: baroque sacred oratorio, harpsichord, strings, timpani, dramatic tenor with full chorus, handelian, building to a blaze
picks.why: Chaos, clashing atoms, then 'Let there be light!' and the sun flaming from his orient bed — written to be sung and knows it.

picks.style: oratorio opening, low strings, thundering timpani, chorus of furies, ominous, accelerating
picks.why: 'Vengeance, arise from thy infernal bed' — a curse, an unchaining of Furies, and a king possessed; a real dramatic opening.

picks.style: consolatory anthem, harp, chamber organ, treble voices with soft chorus, slow, radiant, healing
picks.why: 'Angels, heal his anguish! Your harps and voices join!' — short lines, refrain shape, pure hymn material.

picks.style: colonial american elegy, viola da gamba, acoustic guitar, plaintive tenor, slow, moonlit, tidal
picks.why: Night on the sea-beat shore, the broad moon through broken clouds, anchored navies lifting their shrouds — genuine lyric weather.

picks.style: comic patter song, harpsichord, fiddle, arch soprano, brisk, coy, tart
picks.why: The belle fishing for compliments and closing on 'You're only joking, Mr. Brainless' — a perfect small comic scene in one voice.

picks.style: 18th century satirical air, oboe, fiddle, jaunty baritone, brisk, strutting
picks.why: 'The modish hat, whose breadth contains / The measure of its owner's brains' — the whole beau assembled item by item.

picks.style: delphic oracle chant, aulos, deep drone, breathy female voice answered by low male chorus, slow, uncanny
picks.why: 'I know the number of the grains of sand and the extent of the sea' — the tortoise boiling in bronze; the most famous oracle in the book.

picks.style: spartan war elegy, bowed lyre, single war drum, stark male chorus, very slow, grave, stone-cold
picks.why: Either Sparta wasted or a king of Heracles' line dead — closing on 'go tell the Spartans that we lie here obedient to their commands'.

picks.style: apocalyptic oracle, wailing aulos, low drone, keening female voice, unsettled, gathering dread
picks.why: 'Wretches, why do you linger here?' — the body dismembered limb by limb, roofs running with gore; terrifying and rhythmically relentless.

picks.style: mock-oracular chant, aulos, tambourine, theatrical male voice with heavy reverb, ceremonial, faintly absurd
picks.why: The new god introducing himself — 'Glycon my name, man's light, son's son to Zeus' — pomp with the fraud audible underneath.

picks.style: hieratic incantation, plucked lyre, small cymbals, incense-hazed male voice, slow, portentous
picks.why: 'First thou wast Peleus' son, and next Menander; then thine own self; next, a sunbeam shalt be' — transmigration as sales pitch.

picks.style: mock-scholastic latin chorus, chamber organ, plucked strings, deadpan male voices in unison, moderate, wry, ceremonial
picks.why: Virgil's returning golden age beside Molière's doctors solemnly explaining that opium sends you to sleep by its dormitive virtue.

picks.style: late roman lament, solo lyre, one fragile tenor, very slow, hushed, valedictory, almost unaccompanied
picks.why: Hadrian's dying address to his own soul — five short lines, complete, and among the most quoted in Latin.
